text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least 90 armed cattle rustlers die in a fierce two-day battle with security forces in the volatile Marakwet/Pokot district border in the Rift Valley.
- Electoral Commission chairman Zaccheus Chesoni says plans to restructure the electoral process will save the country 500 million shillings ($9 million).
- A serious food crisis may delay the opening of schools in Turkana District.
- At least 40 people are feared dead after the banks of a seasonal river in the coastal district of Kilifi burst, drowning a whole village.
- Police Commissioner Duncan Wachira escapes with minor injuries from a road accident along the Mombasa-Nairobi road.
- The government issues a final ultimatum on Monday to holders of the old national identification cards to register for new generation IDs.
- Officials of the National Convention Assembly lobbying for constitutional reforms disagree with their provincial representatives over the application of funds intended for a rally last Saturday.
- A Kenyan fishing vessel with 30 crew members aboard has been reported hijacked off the Somali coast by militiamen demanding ransom.
- President Daniel arap Moi mourns the 33 victims who died in a road accident over the weekend.
